question: According to the manual, bus drivers must have a CDL if they drive a vehicle designed to seat how many people, including the driver?
choice_a: 6 or more
choice_b: 16 or more
choice_c: 8 or more
choice_d: 25 or more
explanation: The manual states bus drivers must have a commercial driver's license if they drive a vehicle designed to seat 16 or more people, including the driver.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, Introduction

question: To get the Passenger (P) endorsement, which sections of the manual must you pass a knowledge test on?
choice_a: Sections 3 and 9 only
choice_b: Only Section 4
choice_c: The entire manual, including Section 10
choice_d: Sections 2 and 4, plus Section 5 if the bus has air brakes
explanation: The manual states that to get the P endorsement, you must pass a knowledge test on Sections 2 and 4, and if your bus has air brakes, you must also pass a knowledge test on Section 5.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, Introduction

question: According to the manual, when reviewing the last driver's inspection report before driving a bus, what should you do?
choice_a: Ignore the previous report and conduct your own inspection only
choice_b: Refuse to sign any report that lists a defect, regardless of certification
choice_c: Only sign the report if there were zero defects listed
choice_d: Sign the report if defects have been certified as repaired or certified as not needing repair
explanation: The manual explains that you should only sign the last driver's report if the defects reported have been certified as repaired or certified as not needing to be repaired.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.1 Vehicle Inspection

question: According to the manual, what emergency reflective equipment must a bus have?
choice_a: 3 reflective triangles or at least 6 fuses or 3 liquid burning flares
choice_b: A single reflective triangle only
choice_c: 10 fuses and no triangles
choice_d: No reflective equipment is required on buses
explanation: The manual requires a bus to have a fire extinguisher and emergency reflectors -- 3 reflective triangles or at least 6 fuses or 3 liquid burning flares -- as required by law.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.1.1 Vehicle Systems

question: According to the manual, what tire condition is prohibited on the front wheels of a bus?
choice_a: Radial tires
choice_b: Tires with any visible tread wear
choice_c: Tires manufactured more than one year ago
choice_d: Recapped or re-grooved tires
explanation: The manual specifies that front wheels of a bus must not have recapped or re-grooved tires.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.1.1 Vehicle Systems

question: According to the manual, when should you never drive a bus?
choice_a: With the interior lights off at night
choice_b: With an open emergency exit door or window
choice_c: With the driver's seatbelt fastened
choice_d: With the roof hatches fully closed
explanation: The manual states you should never drive with an open emergency exit door or window, and the Emergency Exit sign must be clearly visible.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.1.3 Bus Interior

question: According to the manual, what must you ensure when securing baggage and freight on a bus?
choice_a: It allows the driver to move freely and allows riders to exit by any window or door in an emergency
choice_b: It blocks the rear emergency exit to prevent unauthorized use
choice_c: It is stacked as high as possible to maximize space
choice_d: It is placed only in the aisle for easy access
explanation: The manual states that secured baggage and freight must allow the driver to move freely and easily and allow riders to exit by any window or door in an emergency.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.2 Loading and Trip Start

question: According to the manual, which of the following must a bus NEVER carry?
choice_a: Division 2.3 poison gas
choice_b: Drugs
choice_c: Small-arms ammunition labeled ORM-D
choice_d: Emergency hospital supplies
explanation: The manual lists Division 2.3 poison gas, liquid Class 6 poison, tear gas, and irritating material among the hazardous materials a bus must never carry, while small-arms ammunition, emergency hospital supplies, and drugs are permitted in limited amounts.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.2.2 Forbidden Hazardous Materials

question: According to the manual, what is the standee line on a bus designed to allow standing?
choice_a: A line indicating the maximum speed allowed on curves
choice_b: A line showing riders where they cannot stand, with all standing riders required to stay behind it
choice_c: A painted line marking where baggage must be stored
choice_d: A boundary marking the driver's seating area only
explanation: The manual defines the standee line as a two-inch line on the floor (or other means) showing riders where they cannot stand; no rider may stand forward of the rear of the driver's seat, and all standing riders must stay behind the line.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.2.3 Standee Line

question: According to the manual, what should you announce when arriving at a destination or intermediate stop?
choice_a: Nothing; announcements are optional
choice_b: Only the bus number
choice_c: The location, reason for stopping, next departure time, and bus number
choice_d: Only the current time
explanation: The manual states that when arriving at a destination or intermediate stop, you should announce the location, reason for stopping, next departure time, and bus number.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.2.4 At Your Destination

question: According to the manual, why should you tell passengers the rules about smoking, vaping, drinking, or using electronic devices at the start of a trip?
choice_a: It is required only on interstate charter trips
choice_b: It is only necessary if the trip is longer than 8 hours
choice_c: It has no effect on passenger behavior
choice_d: Explaining the rules at the start will help avoid trouble later
explanation: The manual states that explaining rules about smoking, vaping, drinking, or electronic devices at the start of the trip will help avoid trouble later.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.3.1 Passenger Supervision

question: According to the manual, what should you do before starting the bus after passengers board or leave at a stop?
choice_a: Ask all riders to stand near the front for balance
choice_b: Wait for them to sit down or brace themselves before starting
choice_c: Sound the horn twice and then depart
choice_d: Start immediately to stay on schedule
explanation: The manual advises waiting for riders to sit down or brace themselves before starting, and making starts and stops as smooth as possible to avoid rider injury.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.3.2 At Stops

question: According to the manual, where do bus crashes often happen?
choice_a: Only on unpaved roads
choice_b: At intersections
choice_c: On long, straight highway stretches
choice_d: Only in parking lots
explanation: The manual states bus crashes often happen at intersections, so drivers should use caution at every intersection even if it has a signal or stop sign controlling other traffic.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.3.3 Common Crashes

question: According to the manual, what does it mean if your bus leans toward the outside on a banked curve?
choice_a: You are driving too fast
choice_b: The bus has a mechanical steering defect
choice_c: It is a normal and safe condition at any speed
choice_d: The road's design speed is too low for any vehicle
explanation: The manual states that if your bus leans toward the outside on a banked curve, you are driving too fast, and that with good traction the bus may roll over while with poor traction it might slide off the curve.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.3.4 Speed on Curves

question: According to the manual, how far before a railroad crossing should a bus stop?
choice_a: At least 200 feet before the crossing
choice_b: Buses are not required to stop at railroad crossings
choice_c: Exactly at the crossing itself
choice_d: Between 15 and 50 feet before the crossing
explanation: The manual instructs bus drivers to stop between 15 and 50 feet before railroad crossings, listen and look both ways for trains, and open the front door if it helps see or hear an approaching train.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.3.5 Railroad-highway Crossing/Stops

question: According to the manual, at which of the following must a bus driver still slow down and carefully check for other vehicles without coming to a full stop?
choice_a: At crossings marked as 'exempt' or 'abandoned'
choice_b: At any crossing with a stopped school bus nearby
choice_c: At every crossing with an active train
choice_d: At any double-track crossing
explanation: The manual lists streetcar crossings, crossings directed by a law enforcement officer or flagman, crossings with a green traffic signal, and crossings marked 'exempt' or 'abandoned' as situations where a bus must slow down and check but does not need to stop.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.3.5 Railroad-highway Crossing/Stops

question: According to the manual, how far before a drawbridge without a signal light or traffic attendant must a bus stop?
choice_a: At least 500 feet before the bridge
choice_b: At least 50 feet before the draw of the bridge
choice_c: Exactly at the edge of the draw
choice_d: Buses are exempt from stopping at drawbridges
explanation: The manual states buses must stop at least 50 feet before the draw of a bridge that lacks a signal light or traffic control attendant, and confirm the draw is completely closed before crossing.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.3.6 Drawbridges

question: According to the manual, what must a driver for an interstate carrier complete at the end of each shift?
choice_a: Only a verbal report to the dispatcher
choice_b: Nothing, unless a defect is found
choice_c: A fuel receipt only
choice_d: A written inspection report listing any defect that would affect safety or cause a breakdown
explanation: The manual requires interstate carrier drivers to complete a written inspection report for each bus, listing any defect that would affect safety or result in a breakdown, and to note if there are no defects.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.4 After-trip Vehicle Inspection

question: According to the manual, what should you avoid doing when fueling a bus with riders on board?
choice_a: Refueling in a closed building with riders on board
choice_b: Using diesel fuel instead of gasoline
choice_c: Turning off the engine before fueling
choice_d: Refueling at any time, even with no riders present
explanation: The manual states you should avoid fueling with riders on board unless necessary, and should never refuel in a closed building with riders on board.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.5 Prohibited Practices

question: According to the manual, when may you tow or push a disabled bus with riders aboard?
choice_a: Only if the bus is less than half full
choice_b: Never, under any circumstances, even if leaving the bus is dangerous
choice_c: At any time, for any distance, as long as speed stays under 10 mph
choice_d: Only to the nearest safe spot to discharge passengers, unless getting off would be unsafe
explanation: The manual states you should not tow or push a disabled bus with riders aboard unless getting off would be unsafe, and then only to the nearest safe spot to discharge passengers.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.5 Prohibited Practices

question: According to the manual, what does a mass transit bus's brake-door interlock system do?
choice_a: It applies the brakes and holds the throttle in idle when the rear door is open, releasing when the door closes
choice_b: It locks the rear door whenever the bus exceeds 35 mph
choice_c: It automatically applies the parking brake at every scheduled stop
choice_d: It shuts off the engine whenever a window is opened
explanation: The manual describes the brake-door interlock as applying the brakes and holding the throttle in idle position when the rear door is open, releasing when the driver closes the rear door.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.6 Use of Brake-door Interlocks

question: According to the manual, can the brake-door interlock system be used in place of the parking brake?
choice_a: No, this safety feature should not be used in place of the parking brake
choice_b: Only when the bus is empty of passengers
choice_c: Yes, but only on buses built after 2015
choice_d: Yes, it is designed as a full replacement for the parking brake
explanation: The manual explicitly states that the brake-door interlock should not be used in place of the parking brake.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 4, 4.6 Use of Brake-door Interlocks
